subject: Marketplace availability phasing & co-sell enablement — AWS / Azure / GCP
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudpartner.io>, Ash Patel <ash.patel@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace availability phasing & co-sell enablement — AWS / Azure / GCP

Team / partners —

Following up from last week's GTM sync: attached is a compact SKU + region proposal for initial marketplace listings across AWS, Azure, and GCP and a suggested co-sell enablement sequence. High-level goals: get a lightweight, clearly packaged set of SKUs available in the top 3 clouds in a phased way so we enable co-sell leads without blowing up certification and listing timelines.

Attachment: marketplace_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx (tabbed: SKU-defs / Cloud-phasing / Pricing-notes)
Also attached: cosell_play_sequence_v1.pdf (proposed handoff sequence and lead routing)

My recommended phasing (summary):
- Phase 0 (pre-list): Private Reserved Dedicated for pilot accounts + Marketplace trial images in US-EAST only (no co-sell) — target: week of May 24
- Phase 1 (core SKU, GA-lite): AWS (us-east/us-west) + Azure (eastus) listing of a single standardized SKU (on-demand compute + 30d retention) — enable co-sell registration with partner portal — target: June 14
- Phase 2 (expanded SKUs): Add GCP (us-central1) and tiered SKUs (burst, high-memory) + EU region listings for customers in EU — target: July 12

Questions for internal owners and Sophie/Ash:
1) Is the AWS co-sell gate (partner registration + APN validation) doable by June 14 if we lock SKU packaging today?
2) Do we need separate licensed vs. BYOL SKUs for Azure initial listing or can we use one unified SKU with a checkbox?
3) Lead routing: who in sales should get first-touch co-sell leads from each cloud? (proposed: Ben owns AWS, Laura owns Azure, Soojin handles GCP pilot)

Please reply with any redlines in the attached matrix — I want to freeze SKU definitions by Friday May 7 so engineering and the marketplace team can start the listing requests.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Cloud GTM, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudpartner.io>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace availability phasing & co-sell enablement — AWS / Azure / GCP

Jonas — thanks for the clear proposal. Quick notes inline.

On 2027-05-04 09:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> My recommended phasing (summary):
> - Phase 0 (pre-list): Private Reserved Dedicated for pilot accounts + Marketplace trial images in US-EAST only (no co-sell) — target: week of May 24
> - Phase 1 (core SKU, GA-lite): AWS (us-east/us-west) + Azure (eastus) listing of a single standardized SKU (on-demand compute + 30d retention) — enable co-sell registration with partner portal — target: June 14
> - Phase 2 (expanded SKUs): Add GCP (us-central1) and tiered SKUs (burst, high-memory) + EU region listings for customers in EU — target: July 12

A few redlines/suggestions:
- For Phase 0, we should make the trial image an AMI + container listing so customers can self-serve a 14-day demo before we list marketplace SKUs. That reduces initial paperwork.
- Phase 1: AWS co-sell timelines are tight. I recommend we treat June 14 as a soft target and commit to "co-sell readiness" (docs + partner packet) by that date; actual APN listing may follow by ~3 weeks depending on APN queue. Let's plan internal enablement earlier (June 7).
- Azure: we should offer a single license SKU initially but publish guidance for BYOL customers; Azure Marketplace reviewers prefer clear manifests — engineering needs to confirm image/container format by May 10.
- GCP: gating item is IAM+billing account mapping for resellers — recommend we postpone GCP listing to late July unless we prioritize a pilot customer.

Action items I can own: assemble APN checklist, confirm image formats with infra, and draft the co-sell lead routing play (internal handoff + SFDC fields) by May 10.

If we all agree on: 1) freeze SKU definitions by May 7, 2) finalize image artifacts by May 10, I'll push the marketplace requests the following week.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudpartner.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ash Patel <ash.patel@enterprisecorp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T13:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace availability phasing & co-sell enablement — AWS / Azure / GCP

Jonas / Soojin — good plan. A few notes from the partner side:

- AWS co-sell: we can fast-track co-sell enablement if Redwood submits a "co-sell intake" and provides the partner packet + two reference customers. If you can provide the packet by June 7, APN team will prioritize review and we typically see a 2–3 week turnaround.
- Azure certification: Azure Marketplace has a validation step on package size and network config. A single SKU with a BYOL option works fine; please ensure the manifest clearly states data residency and AI compute requirements.
- Lead routing: we can wire a webhook from Partner Portal to your SFDC. The webhook payload needs: deal id, cloud marketplace, SKU id, customer email, and lead type (trial/demo/co-sell). Ben's team owning AWS looks good; we recommend a secondary owner (soak) for EU leads.

Small ask: could you add "minimum supported sequence" column to your SKU matrix (i.e., what artifacts we need to prove for co-sell: docs, EULA, reference, security checklist)? That helps us triage listing priority.

Happy to join a 30-minute review on Friday if you want to walk the matrix live.

Cheers,
Sophie Park
Partner Lead, CloudPartner Network
sophie.park@cloudpartner.io

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudpartner.io>, Ash Patel <ash.patel@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace availability phasing & co-sell enablement — AWS / Azure / GCP

Thanks everyone — aligned on approach. Summary and agreed calls-to-action: 

1) Freeze SKU defs by EOD Friday May 7 — Soojin to push final edits to the matrix; Ben/Laura to confirm pricing tiers. (Owner: Soojin; ETA: 2027-05-07T17:00:00-07:00)
2) Engineering to produce AMI + container artifacts by May 10 (Owner: infra; item added to engineering backlog)
3) Sophie will accept a partner packet + two references to submit the AWS co-sell intake (Owner: Jonas / Marketing)
4) We will push Azure manifest review week of May 10 — Laura to coordinate with product security for the manifest checklist (Owner: Laura; ETA: 2027-05-12)
5) GCP listing will be scoped as Phase 2 unless a pilot customer requires earlier listing (Owner: Soojin)

I attached an updated matrix with a new column "minimum_supported_sequence" and a draft lead webhook spec. If there are no objections I will: 1) update the HubSpot deal with the new milestones, and 2) schedule a 30-min review with Sophie on Friday May 7 10:00am PT.

Attachments: marketplace_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated), cosell_play_sequence_v1.pdf (lead webhook spec included)

If you're OK, I'll lock the export and mark the SKU sheet as final.

Thanks — looking forward to getting AWS first listings into queue.

Jonas
